title: Inside Bolo AI: Building a Voice Assistant with Flutter and Gemini
excerpt: How I combined Flutter, Supabase, and Gemini to create a voice assistant that automates devices.

content.text: When I started building Bolo AI, the goal was simple: let users control their smart devices using natural language, without juggling multiple apps.
I used Flutter's microphone plugin to capture audio, then converted it to text with a lightweight speech‑to‑text model running locally. This kept latency low and respected privacy.
The transcribed text is sent to Gemini, which returns a structured intent. I designed a prompt that asks for JSON output, making parsing straightforward.
Supabase stores conversation history, allowing the assistant to reference previous commands. Row‑level security ensures each user's data remains isolated.
For offline capability, I cached device states in HiveDB. When a command arrives, the app first checks the local cache, then syncs with the cloud when connectivity returns.
The best voice assistants feel invisible.
content.author: Roshan Lal Yogi

content.text: I learned that even a 200‑millisecond delay can break the conversational flow. By pre‑warming the Gemini client and batching small requests, I reduced average response time by 30%.
